answer: Tasks are committed before their inputs are derived from a specified future drand quicknet pulse. Its threshold-BLS signature is publicly verifiable yet unpredictable at commitment time, preventing precomputation or offline work stockpiling across sybil keys. Each key must answer fresh pulse-bound inputs such as wharf, dune, or ferrous before a deadline; validators recompute the derivation and check the commitment. This limits work reuse, though randomness alone does not prove unique identity.
